_comment: Maintained by Claude — see ../CLAUDE.md 'Dashboard Maintenance' rule. Status values: concept | in-progress | review | ready | archived. Keys in 'mocks' are folder paths relative to products/Scheduling/ (no trailing /index.html).

recentChanges.summary: Dashboard now supports an optional per-mock 'extraLinks' array (companion pages living beside index.html) — rendered as a labeled URL row plus a secondary button on the card. Used it to surface the Event Indicator's 'Current UI' page so the team can open it from the dashboard. Also tightened the wrapped-line spacing inside current-ui.html's hover card (Concurrent assignment / Lists) so a multi-line value reads as one grouped item.

Added a 'Current UI' companion page reproducing the live production Vector Scheduling day view (the 'before' next to the UX-2474 redesign): production topnav/toolbar/date-nav, green C SHIFT bar, near-square station/assignment cards, and the black detail hover-card. The hover-card showcases the new UX-2474 info in production styling — all uniform right-aligned rows split into up to three divider-separated sections (credential qualifiers / concurrent shift / admin metadata, each omitted when empty): credential status with index-matching icons (expired = red ✕ circle, expiring = yellow ⚠ triangle, missing = red dashed ? — icon inside the credential-colored badge), the concurrent shift (flag + type, then assignment name with its time on one line beneath), then Work type / Last modified by / On / Last update / Recurrence start / Covering For / Lists / Phone. Schedule-row qualifier badges match the index (colored badge + status icon) and sit above the name with the orange concurrent flag inline before the name; hover badge sizing matches the row badge exactly.

Expanded the concurrent-shift flag in the staff card's detail drawer to show the other shift the employee is scheduled on at the same time — its type plus the assignment and time — instead of just the type label. Added data-concurrent-assignment/data-concurrent-time to the five flagged cards.

Added stable ids (rule-builder, rule-builder-chat, rule-builder-config) to the dual-screen builder's containers so feedback comment-widget pins anchor reliably on this React view instead of drifting/breaking when the screen remounts.

Pinned the 'Who accepts' picker + Run callback button to the bottom of the screen in embedded Preview Mode (added a flex spacer so the bar no longer slides down as callback-chain steps accumulate). Replaced the native 'Who accepts' <select> with a custom WhoAcceptsSelect dropdown that opens upward over the chain, so its options stay visible above the bottom-pinned trigger.

In embedded Preview Mode, removed the standalone 'Predicted call order' roster (it's now redundant with the Preview Ranking / Rule Summary box on that page) and made that box's Preview Ranking list reflect the live simulation instead of the static rule preview: rows re-order as callbacks are accepted, accrued hours roll into each total, ineligible people (PTO/sick/on-shift) gray out, and whoever the simulation just granted hours to shows a green '+Nh' badge. The full-page standalone simulator keeps its original roster (scoped the removal with `!panelOnly`). PreviewRankingList/RuleSummary now take an optional `ranking` prop.

Moved the live Preview Ranking / Rule Summary box out of the rule builder's config panel — it now appears only when Preview Mode opens (it was already rendered inside the embedded simulator). The builder's sticky header is reduced to just the skipped-questions 'revisit before saving' nudge, and the top-ranked 'Next' employee pill stays in the panel header. Removed the now-unused stickyOpen state and its scroll-collapse listener.

While adding a new rule (the dual split-screen builder view), the outer navbar and the top heading header bar are now hidden — `{!building && <OuterSidebar/>}` and `{!building && <TopBar/>}` in the App shell (the sub-sidebar was already hidden during building). The builder's chat + config/preview panes now run full-bleed, and the chrome returns when you exit the builder.

Preview Mode is now EMBEDDED in the rule builder instead of loading a full new page. The dual-screen builder layout is unchanged — same AI chat on the left, same 460px right panel — the ONLY difference is the right panel's contents swap from the Rule Configuration form to the live callback simulator. Clicking Preview ranking / Preview Mode does the swap while the AI chat stays on the left; the chat drops an 'Entering preview mode' note with an 'Exit preview' chip, and the user can leave via that chip, by typing 'exit', or via the panel's Exit button (the header button also toggles Preview Mode ⇄ Exit Preview). SimulatorView gained a `panelOnly` prop that hides its full-page banner and its own left chat/settings column, stretches the callback-chain column to full width, and prepends a compact settings strip (shift start date picker, duration, wait-time/candidate toggle) plus the Preview Ranking + Rule Summary box (RuleSummary is now published to window so the simulator block can render it). The standalone Approaches & Rules 'Preview Mode' button still opens the full-page simulator.

Rule builder + Preview Mode pass. (1) The fresh-build chat now opens by asking how to set up — 'Guided setup', 'Give me a description', or 'Upload my MOU' — and routes accordingly; the guided path's first question is 'Which employees would you like to apply rules to?'. (2) The rule CONFIG panel gained a 'Callback Method' field (Wait time vs. Candidate method, as radios with descriptions) in the Callback delivery section — it's a rule-config choice, so it also surfaces in the Rule Summary; the simulator's Callback Settings keeps its original plain 'Wait time: N minutes' field. (3) The predicted-call-order roster now leads with each person's accrued hours as a big number instead of the rank circle (rank moved to a small #N in the meta line); accepting a callback adds the shift Duration to that person's hours and shows a green '+8h' badge. (4) The callback chain's completed step circles (and history rows) are clickable for a read-only revisit that highlights the run without rewinding; each run logs the accepter's '+Nh' accrual. (5) The shift Start field is now a real date picker and displays the ACTIVE callback date, which advances one day per run so the chain simulates calling on successive days; picking a new date resets the chain to that day.

Replaced the vertical setup checklist on Approaches & Rules with a horizontal three-step stepper (Create approaches → Create rules → Ready to send out callbacks). Circular badges connected by progress lines that turn green as each step completes; the active step gets a purple gradient circle with a glow ring + NEXT pill; the helper paragraph sits in a tinted hint row below. After Save Rule, 'Create rules' checks off and 'Ready to send out callbacks' becomes the active step with its own helper body and a primary 'Send out new callback' button right in the hint row. Once the user opens any existing rule for editing, `setupAcknowledged` flips true at App level and the stepper hides on return — the methodology card expands to full row width because it sits in a flex:1 column with no sibling. The Rules card empty state is replaced with the saved rule as a clickable tile so the editing flow works end-to-end.

Embedded the new shared feedback widget on every Scheduling mock — Rules engine only, AI search engine dashboard, Theme Colors, Event Indicator UX-2474, test, and dashboard each now load /commentwidget/feedback-widget.js before </body>. The widget adds a bottom-right 'Add feedback' toolbar; click an element to drop a pin, add a comment, reply in a thread, mark done, or delete. All pin state is shared via a Cloudflare Worker + KV (no login flow — just a name typed once), and every action also logs to the team Confluence page as a permanent receipt.

Pulled the three-step setup checklist out of the methodology header into its own standalone box on the right side of the methodology card. The two cards now sit side-by-side in a flex row with `alignItems: stretch` so they match heights: methodology accordion on the left (illustrations and tile cards shrunk to ~96×70px so it fits beside the wider helper), setup helper box on the right (380px wide). The helper has a 'Setup checklist' title with a clipboard-check icon, an 'N of 3' progress badge, a purple progress bar, and a vertical list of the three steps (Create approaches → Create rules → Send out callback). The active step expands to a two-line layout with a helper paragraph under the label explaining HOW + WHAT (e.g. for Create rules: 'Rules decide who gets called first — by accumulated hours, seniority, a Rolodex rotation, or a custom factor. Tap Add New Rule with AI in the Rules box below…'). Done = green check + strike-through, active = purple ring + filled dot + bold label + 'NEXT' badge + helper paragraph, pending = grey outline. The whole row disappears once every step is checked. The Rules card still hides its grid + Preview Mode button while no rules exist, swapping in a dashed-outline empty state with a sparkle icon, 'No rules yet — let's create your first one' headline, helper copy pointing to the gradient '+ Add New Rule with AI' button, and a curved hint arrow drawing the eye up to that CTA.

Redesigned the callback methodology again, this time as a row of five tinted illustration cards connected by horizontal dotted lines — replaces the hub-and-spoke diagram. Each card has a unique inline SVG illustration: 1) three person silhouettes with the middle one circled and a green checkmark (Select an approach, blue), 2) a central orange gear with unsorted bars on the left and sorted 1st/2nd bars on the right (Apply a rule, orange), 3) a document with three ranked list rows + sparkle badge (Calling list generated, purple), 4) a phone with sound waves on both sides + green check speech bubble (Crew Scheduler reaches out, green), 5) ascending bar chart with an upward trend arrow and marker dot (Rankings adjust live, blue). A numbered gradient badge tucks at each card's top-left and a 'Five steps from picking who's eligible to filling a shift.' intro line sits above the row. Compact sizing (130×96px cards) so the accordion doesn't dominate the page.

Approaches and Rules lists both render as auto-fill CSS grids now (Approaches ~240px tiles, Rules ~300px since rule descriptions need more room) so multiple items sit side-by-side on a row instead of one tall column. Moved the Active / Archived tab bar from above the Approaches header into the header itself, immediately below the description — makes it visually obvious the tabs only filter approaches (the Rules card below has no archive view). Pulled the 'Add New Approach' and gradient 'Add New Rule with AI' buttons up to the right side of each card's title row, so each header surfaces its primary action right next to the title. Rules header keeps Preview Mode + Add New Rule with AI together on the right. Redesigned the callback methodology as a hub-and-spoke illustration: two input nodes on the left (Select Approach, Apply Rule) and two output nodes on the right (Employees Notified, Rankings Adjust) flow via gradient curved bezier paths into a large central AI hub with concentric dashed rings, a radial teal gradient sphere, and an 'AI' badge. The composition is backed by overlapping soft cloud gradients, scattered sparkle dots and 4-point twinkles in SVG, and the input/output icons sit on slightly tilted gradient tiles — reads as an infographic illustration instead of a linear stepper.

Rule builder follow-ups: moved 'Bring in a Rules file' from outside the rules list into the chat's rule-type suggestions block; stacked the multi-select chat chips vertically (one per row) instead of the dense wrapping grid; made the 'Custom answer' callout bigger and more prominent (purple ring + downward arrow) so users see clearly that the textarea below is the next step. Every manual edit on the right configuration panel now records itself in the chat with an 'edited in panel' tag and a generic 'Got it — let's build on top of that' AI reply, while the field-highlight pulse is now reserved for chat-driven updates only. Added a new 'How should we reach employees?' callback-delivery section to the config panel: pick a channel (Phone Call / Text / Push Notification); each channel exposes its own cadence menu (e.g. 'Call again in 4 hours' vs 'Push every 15 minutes' vs 'Push everyone all at once'); a 'Retry the next day if unfilled?' radio + a per-channel next-day cadence menu cover the second-day recovery rhythm.

Replaced the inline AI rule-builder banner on Approaches & Rules with a compact gradient 'New Rule' primary button (mirrors the 'Add New Approach' placement). Clicking it opens the dual-configure rule builder where the chat now leads with 'Which approach(es) should this rule apply to?' before showing the template suggestions. Also enlarged the 'How does callback ranking work?' accordion header (it's now the primary label), removed the redundant 'CallBack Methodology' tag, added a 'Diagram' pill, and a caption clarifying the visual is a reference diagram and not an interactive stepper.

Preview Mode rework: left panel now has AI Chat / Callback Settings tabs; right panel starts empty until both Approach and Rule are picked, then populates the AI summary in chat and the predicted call order on the right; right panel reflowed so the stepper + callback chain results sit at the top, the predicted call order list below, and the 'who accepts' dropdown + Run callback button stay anchored at the bottom; on-shift employees are sorted to the bottom of the list AND grayed out (they can't take a callback while already working) and are excluded from the eligible pool.

Renamed 'CrewSense' to 'Crew Scheduler' in the CallBack Methodology step ('Crew Scheduler sends the call') across both the Rules engine prototype and the test mock — aligns labeling with current product naming.

Rule builder + Preview Mode overhaul: swapped the '+' glyph to a sparkles icon on every 'Add new rule' surface; hide the sub-sidebar when the rule builder owns the screen (focus mode); fixed A&R page-level scrolling (removed the inner card's overflow:hidden trap); all configurable fields now render on the right-side panel from the start with the same highlight pulse when chat fills them in. Chat now answers 'What is <rule type>?' inline with an AI tutor explanation; 'Save rule' / 'Preview ranking' / 'Adjust something' end-of-flow chips are wired to commit/save, jump into Preview, and ask 'What would you like to change?' with the change-menu chips. A Preview Mode button appears in the builder header once minimum info is in. Preview Mode now shows a horizontal stepper for the callback chain (#1 → #N) and the per-step 'System decides / Someone else accepted' radios collapsed into a single dropdown — 'Random (system decides)' as the first option, followed by every available person. Sim chat auto-scrolls to the latest AI answer.

AI search engine dashboard.description: Conversational AI search interface for the CallBack scheduling dashboard.

Event Indicator UX-2474.description: Rethinking how events are grouped and indicated on the scheduling calendar. Includes a 'Current UI' companion page (current-ui.html) reproducing the live production day view as the 'before' comparison.

Rules engine only.description: Standalone rules engine view for configuring scheduling automations and constraints.

test.description: Vanilla HTML / Vector-components port of the Rules Engine CallBack prototype — same purple AI gradients and friendly chip palettes, no React.

Theme Colors.description: System settings page for customizing theme, brand colors, and nav appearance.
